title: Long delay echoes rise when Earth-Moon L5 is above the horizon

tellings.quote: And one study even found a statistically significant increase in LDEs when the Earth-Moon L5 Lagrange point was above the horizon.

plain: Radio operators have sometimes heard their own signals come back seconds after sending them. These are called long delay echoes, and one study supposedly found more of them whenever a certain point in space was above the horizon. That point is the Earth-Moon L5 point, a spot along the Moon's orbit where an object can stay parked because the pulls of Earth and Moon balance out. Michels mentions the study without naming it, and it matters because it would hint that something sitting there is bouncing the signals back.
